Recent notes

  • A and C angles: in-situ calibration and the is2_v2 re-pass 2026-10-12TrackingCalibration

    The two-sided is2_v2 re-pass confirms ×1.49 (A) and ×1.82 (C) more tracks on the wall than production. Open: the capsule focus asks for is2 angles ×1.12 (A) / ×1.12 (C) while in-beam muons read them right; geometry, source offset, depth origin and the kernel are ruled out. Next steps to settle it.

  • MX17 response simulation, animated 2026-10-12SimulationAnimation

    One muon through the whole simulation chain (Geant4 → Magboltz drift → Garfield avalanche and ions → resistive induction → DREAM → FEU → wft), which code does each part, and how its pulse compares with the real det3 average. Toggle the ion signal to see the T14 rise-time problem.

  • MX17 response simulation: state of play (Oct 2026) 2026-10-12SimulationT14

    The Geant4 → Garfield → induction → DREAM chain vs det3 cosmics: charge ×1.6 low, gain slope ×1.5 shallow, pulses too slow. An independent toy clears the code; the shaper is confirmed 180 ns, so the ion signal must be ≈ 5× suppressed, with no mechanism found.

  • SPS det4 constants on the bench: attachment does not spoil them 2026-10-11Beam testMicromegasGasAttachment

    Injection test of the SPS measurement code with the run_71 O₂ loss on and off: footprint, resistive spread and c2/c1 move ≤ 7 %. What the bench model takes from SPS, and the bench-side degeneracy that remains.

  • Beam gas attachment: the observable and one model for beam and bench 2026-10-10Beam testMicromegasGasAttachment

    det4 at H4 loses late drift charge at the same rate per ns at three fields, both views, no undershoot: O₂ attachment (~150–290 ppm). The June bench, same model, six fields: no O₂. Slides.

  • MX17 papers: the two-paper plan 2026-10-10DetectorPaper

    The detector paper split into two companions (detector & performance; reconstruction with a hits-vs-waveforms comparison): outlines, work left, order of work, n_TOF tripwires.
